keyVerseText: All the days of the vow of his separation there shall no razor come upon his head: until the days be fulfilled, in the which he separateth himself unto the LORD, he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew root פָּרַע (pâraʻ) underlying פֶּרַע (peraʻ) carries the core idea of loosening, uncovering, or letting go. This root sense extends metaphorically to leading or acting as a leader, suggesting a dynamic of release or freedom that accompanies authority. Thus, the literal sense of פֶּרַע as 'locks' or 'hair let loose' reflects a tangible expression of this root concept—hair that is unbound or exposed, symbolizing both physical and figurative freedom or distinction beyond a mere physical description.
usageInScripture: The term פֶּרַע appears only twice in Scripture, consistently referring to the hair or locks of the head. Translations such as 'and shall let the locks' and 'nor suffer their locks' emphasize the literal meaning of unbound or disheveled hair. This consistency in usage underscores its primary semantic range as physical hair, with an added nuance of leadership or prominence in some contexts, as seen in the lexicon's note on 'leader.' The word thus bridges the concrete image of hair with a symbolic role of status or identity.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding פֶּרַע enriches our grasp of biblical symbolism where physical states often reflect spiritual realities. The notion of 'letting the locks grow' or 'unbinding hair' can signify consecration, separation, or a visible mark of devotion to God, as hair becomes a sign of holiness or leadership. This aligns with the biblical theme that outward appearance can mirror inward commitment and divine calling. Recognizing the root meaning of loosening or leading invites believers to see Christ as the ultimate leader who liberates and consecrates His people, calling them to live visibly distinct lives set apart for God's purposes.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 6:5 commands that during the vow of separation, no razor shall touch the head, allowing the locks to grow freely. Here, פֶּרַע conveys more than just hair; it symbolizes a physical sign of holiness and dedication to the LORD. The verse highlights how letting the hair grow uncut is an act of consecration, a visible testimony of one's commitment and separation unto God. This word deepens the understanding of the Nazirite vow as an embodied spiritual discipline marked by the unloosed locks.
